chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Ragtime piano players Spikes heard in his travels
summary: Spikes recalls ragtime pianists in the West, including Gene Thomas, Wesley Fields, Sid LaProtty and Jockey Bill of Prescott, and says it was all blues.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: How about...did you run into any local jazz bands or musicians in any of these travels that...

No, they wasn't playin'...they called it ragtime in those days. All the piano players was ragtime piano players, y'know. They played all like Scott Joplin and those guys, y'know. They played all ragtime. Strictly ragtime.
Was there anybody--any ragtime players that really stood out in your memory? Anbody who was exceptionally good that you ran across in your travels?

Yeah, but I don't remember their names...two, three I know...there was a fellow in...in, I think, Denver...Bisbee...named Gene Thomas, and, uh...now, I'm...if you go up to Frisco, yeah, there was a Fields--Wesley Fields. And Sid LaProtty that was a piano
player with us in that band in there, and there were several of them-- ragtime piano players around there. O'course, that was back in '15... '16, which you want before that.
Well, I want it all but I was asking you about the early ones first.

Well, the early ones first--I know Jockey Bill in Prescott. I remember him. He played a lot of old ragtime things but he had a wonderful tenor voice. Gee, he was beautiful. I mean, he called him Jockey Bill because, even when he was so small, he used to ...he was a little guy but he hung around the races until he got... until he started playing piano for a living and everything, and he was singing and playing in the saloons. He had a beautiful voice, and he played that old ragtime stuff. It's all blues, you know, in those days. They called it ragtime but it's the same blues thing over and over and over...always that blue note in it. And I know two, three I can remember in my mind but I can't...can't get their names... what old ragtime piano player...
